text: One of those buyers was an Atlanta businessman named Asa Candler. By 1891, he controlled the whole thing. The total price, by the usual count: about two thousand three hundred dollars.
Candler wasn't a chemist. He was a salesman. And he understood something simple: nobody buys a drink they've never tasted.
So he gave it away. The company handed out and mailed tickets for a free glass. By its own later estimate, between 1894 and 1913, about one in nine Americans got a free Coca-Cola this way.
Then he made sure you couldn't forget the name. It went on clocks, calendars, serving trays, paper fans... anything that would hang on a wall or sit on a counter.
By 1895, Coca-Cola was sold in every state. And in the early 1900s, the cocaine was taken out of the coca leaf extract.
Candler had built a hit at the soda fountain. Now he was about to make one of the strangest deals in business history.
